citation: Labonte CC, et al. Plasma amino acids vs conventional predictors of insulin resistance measured by the hyperinsulinemic clamp. J Endocr Soc 2017;1:861-873.
protocol: Hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic isoaminoacidaemic clamp with isotope tracers: human insulin 40 mU/m2/min (about 1 mU/kg FFM/min) after a postabsorptive baseline, glucose clamped at 5.5 mmol/L (8.0 in some T2D), kinetics from last 30 min of each steady state.
population: Healthy men n=29 (age 53, BMI 23.3) and healthy women n=22 (age 47, BMI 22.3), printed separately from overweight/obese and T2D groups (total 134, 98% Caucasian).
note: Take only the healthy columns; groups are separate. Clamp-state glucose, insulin, FFA and glucagon are not in the table, only fasting values and Rd; clamp insulin appears once in the text as a pooled 560 +/- 10 pmol/L (label unclear).
